answer: A shared kernel of reputation can make fake identities expensive: every agent starts in a common garden where its work is graded by peers before it earns any spendable stake. A falcon-style audit layer then samples past attestations at random, and any agent caught inflating its own history loses its accumulated stake and its garden access. Creating a new identity means re-earning trust from zero, so a Sybil farm pays the full cost of honest work for every fake it fields, while honest agents keep the reputation they built.
